# Method provenance and code availability

<!-- Generated by scripts/check-method-catalog.py; edit method-catalog.json instead. -->

The catalog records method provenance, software availability, and bounded validation evidence. Passing its checker is not evidence of universal statistical validity, application validity, or scientific novelty.

## How to read the catalog

- **Paper-defined** means the mathematical quantity or estimator is taken directly from a cited primary source.
- **Paper-derived** means the implementation composes or adapts published components; the exact composition is not asserted to be a published estimator.
- **Project-defined** means a local diagnostic, workflow, API contract, adapter, or software facility.
- **Implementation origin** is `local-implementation` for code written in this repository, `binding` for a language wrapper, `external` for pinned validation-only code, and `not-implemented` for an explicit negative capability.
- For software references, the displayed year is the year of the pinned validation revision, not a claim about project inception.
- **`depends_on` semantics:** depends_on lists curated method-level dependencies whose estimand, implementation, or scientific status materially constrains the row; it is not an exhaustive source-level call graph. Stable rows may depend only on stable rows; experimental software can compose a research-only estimator only when the stricter scientific boundary is explicit in its constraints.
- **Rust entry-point semantics:** Rust entry points are curated public call sites for each scientific row, not an exhaustive API inventory. release-scope-1.0.json is authoritative for the complete exported-symbol set and its feature/stability boundary.
- **Python entry-point semantics:** Python entry points record callable, class, and policy-attribute availability. The pid_core_rs.experimental.migration surface is exhaustively inventoried in its software row; configurable wrappers may appear on multiple scientific rows, and that prefix denotes an experimental compatibility surface rather than the stability of the wrapped Rust family. cargo_features records pid-core gates; binding rows state the separate pid-python build feature in their constraints.
- **New in pid-rs** describes repository engineering and packaging only. Every row records `scientific_novelty_claim = none`.
- Validation levels are bounded evidence labels. Reference agreement, tests, and formal checks do not establish universal statistical or application validity.

## Explicitly unsupported methods

These rows are negative capability declarations. They do not indicate a roadmap or an implicit endorsement.

| Method | Why it is unsupported | Relevant context |
|---|---|---|
| `unsupported.generic-knn-bootstrap-ci` — Generic calibrated kNN bootstrap confidence intervals | pid-rs does not provide a generic calibrated bootstrap confidence interval for KSG-family estimators because coverage depends on support, dependence, tuning, and estimator regime. | [Hans R. Künsch (1989)](https://doi.org/10.1214/aos/1176347265) |
| `unsupported.hyperbolic-shared-exclusions-pid` — Hyperbolic shared-exclusions PID | pid-rs implements hyperbolic geometry and a research pairwise KSG adaptation, but no hyperbolic shared-exclusions redundancy or PID lattice. | [Maximilian Nickel et al. (2018)](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v80/nickel18a.html); [David A. Ehrlich et al. (2024)](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevE.110.014115) |
| `unsupported.mixed-support-continuous-pid` — General mixed-variable shared-exclusions estimator gap | A paper-defined mixed-variable shared-exclusions functional exists, but pid-rs implements no practical general estimator for arbitrary atomic, mixed, singular, quantized, or unknown population support. | [Chiara Barà et al. (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1103/58bg-5n9s); [Kyle Schick-Poland et al. (2021)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.12393); [David A. Ehrlich et al. (2024)](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevE.110.014115) |

## Method details

These sections render every catalog field. Dependencies follow the curated semantics above and are not an exhaustive source call graph.

### `co-information.continuous-raw` — Raw continuous KSG co-information

Raw continuous co-information obtained by inclusion-exclusion over KSG mutual-information estimates.

- **Classification:** category `measure`; definition `paper-derived`; implementation `local-implementation`; status `research-only`; code availability `local`.
- **Cargo features:** `experimental-continuous`.
- **Rust entry points:** `pid_core::experimental::continuous::raw_scalars::co_information_pairwise`, `pid_core::experimental::continuous::raw_scalars::co_information_triplet`.
- **Python entry points:** `pid_core_rs.experimental.migration.compute_co_information`.
- **Source files:** `crates/pid-core/src/ci.rs`.
- **Source marker files:** `crates/pid-core/src/ci.rs`.
- **Release-scope families:** `pid-core.research.raw-co-information`.
- **Curated dependencies:** `mutual-information.ksg1-raw`.

Bell (2003)](https://www.rd.ntt/cs/team_project/icl/signal/ica2003/cdrom/data/0187.pdf) (`defining-paper`; co-information name, inclusion-exclusion definition, and sign convention); [William J. - **Papers/reference code:** [Weihao Gao et al. (2018)](https://doi.org/10.1109/TIT.2018.2807481) (`methodological-background`; KSG assumptions that Gaussian smoothing alone does not establish)
- **External code pin:** —.
- **New in pid-rs:** Adds typed identities for the ideal kernel, scientific declaration, logical stream, exact matrix buffers, and generated application. It binds fixed preprocessing outputs and caller-declared row-resampling contexts.
- **Scientific novelty claim:** `none`.
- **Constraints:** Added Gaussian noise changes the estimand. Use it only for an explicit observation-noise model or a named seeded scale-sensitivity study.<br>The ideal nondegenerate Gaussian kernel gives the declared population law a smooth positive density with full support in the ambient Euclidean space. It does not establish finite mutual information, independent and identically distributed rows, KSG validity, calibrated uncertainty, or PID-atom monotonicity.<br>For a fixed effective seed, the generated binary64 matrix is deterministic. It is not a population law, and exact replay requires compatible floating-point elementary-function behavior.<br>Separate pseudodraw streams do not establish probabilistic or cryptographic independence.<br>The stream-selection declaration covers the base seed, logical-matrix identity, and stream-domain identity. Each value must satisfy the declared selection rule.<br>A declared row-resampling context binds the index digest and exact input matrix as separate facts. It does not prove that the indices produced the matrix.<br>Separate per-matrix declarations do not establish a joint population-noise model across sources and a target.
- **Bounded validation:** `unit-and-integration` — Private construction, identity-domain separation, finite-input exclusion from stream derivation, finite-input binding, logical-matrix and resampling-context separation, common and separate scale-pseudodraw streams, fixed seed vectors, serialization vocabulary, resources, cancellation, and numerical failures. Limitations: Identity, determinism, and binding tests do not prove the caller's population model, cross-platform bit identity, finite mutual information, estimator consistency, or sensitivity-study conclusions. Evidence: `crates/pid-core/tests/observation_noise.rs`.

- **New in pid-rs:** Makes realization-level and empirical-PMF-averaged SxPID atoms non-interchangeable in Rust and carries an explicit, revisioned measure, aggregation, and standalone-inference boundary through Rust serialization and stable Python objects.
- **Scientific novelty claim:** `none`.
- **Constraints:** A pointwise atom belongs to one distinct positive-mass joint realization under the complete supplied PMF; it is not an intrinsic annotation of one raw input row.<br>An averaged atom is the supplied empirical-PMF probability-weighted plug-in average of corresponding pointwise components; it is not generally a mutual information, a population expectation, or an unbiased population estimate.<br>A standalone atom does not identify its concrete antichain or named coordinate and, for a pointwise atom, its realization; preserve the containing result or pointwise record.<br>Categorical results embed row-count, encoding, observed-cardinality, and occupancy metadata but not source/target names, full matrix shapes, or input hashes; callers or run logs must preserve that data identity separately.<br>The interpretation envelope names the shared-exclusions SxPID measure; its atom values are not measure-independent PID coordinates.<br>The fixed exclusion list is a project-defined claim boundary for contract revision 1; omission of an unrelated inference is not an endorsement.<br>Extracting a bare floating-point component discards the typed interpretation metadata.
- **Bounded validation:** `property-and-integration` — Distinct Rust atom types, derived net identity, exact serialized measure/scope/guard spellings, fixed project-origin exclusion set, bitwise row-permutation determinism, empirical averaging reconstruction, and stable Python parity. Limitations: Nominal types and in-band metadata make scope loss explicit but cannot stop a caller from extracting and relabelling a bare scalar; tests do not establish causal, intentional, normative, or responsibility semantics. Evidence: `crates/pid-core/tests/sxpid_interpretation.rs`, `crates/pid-python/tests/test_v1.py`.

### `unsupported.mixed-support-continuous-pid` — General mixed-variable shared-exclusions estimator gap

The general arbitrary-support shared-exclusions functional is paper-defined, but pid-rs implements neither a general estimator nor the restricted Barà discrete-target/continuous-sources method.

- **Classification:** category `unsupported`; definition `paper-defined`; implementation `not-implemented`; status `unsupported`; code availability `none`.
- **Cargo features:** —.
- **Rust entry points:** —.
- **Python entry points:** —.
- **Source files:** —.
- **Source marker files:** `crates/pid-core/src/pid3.rs`.
- **Release-scope families:** —.
- **Curated dependencies:** —.
- **Papers/reference code:** [Chiara Barà et al. (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1103/58bg-5n9s) (`caveat`; restricted practical estimator for a discrete target and continuous sources); [Kyle Schick-Poland et al. (2021)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.12393) (`defining-paper`; measure-theoretic shared-exclusions PID functional for arbitrary variable types); [David A. Ehrlich et al. (2024)](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevE.110.014115) (`caveat`; continuous estimator support domain)
- **External code pin:** —.
- **New in pid-rs:** Records the estimator/code gap explicitly and directs callers with quantized data to a distinct categorical estimand instead of silently applying full-dimensional continuous code.
- **Scientific novelty claim:** `none`.
- **Constraints:** A paper-defined mixed-variable shared-exclusions functional exists, but pid-rs implements no practical general estimator for arbitrary atomic, mixed, singular, quantized, or unknown population support.<br>Barà et al. provide a restricted discrete-target/continuous-sources nearest-neighbor PID estimator; that method is not implemented in pid-rs.
- **Bounded validation:** `not-validated` — Negative capability declaration. Limitations: Unsupported by design. Evidence: —.
